name: Marcus T.
text: This is interesting but I've actually seen the opposite work better for luxury goods. When we tested $99 vs $97 on our premium skincare line, $99 converted higher. Maybe it depends on the market segment?

name: Elena R.
text: The charm pricing thing feels outdated honestly. Our customers barely notice the difference between $97 and $99 anymore. We've had better results focusing on value communication instead.

name: James K.
text: We tested this exact thing last quarter on our DTC fashion site. $97 beat $99 by about 3% in conversion. Might seem small but that added up to $12k extra revenue over a month.

name: Sofia N.
text: Great breakdown of the psychology here. One question though - did you test this across different traffic sources? I wonder if paid ad audiences react differently than organic.

name: David C.
text: Solid article but I think the real lever is testing with YOUR audience, not just following conventional wisdom. We're a DTC brand and our data showed no statistical difference between the two.
